scope: Approved canonical BAR expansion applied; this is not plan acceptance or shipment evidence

appliedReadback.remainingGate: P-544 / D-076 still requires a measured usable trial configuration under $20/month including compute, disks, backups, network, control plane and inference.

criteria.title: Agent counts come from measurement on real GCP machines

intent.request: Tell users how many Claude/Codex agents each machine size supports, measured on real GCP instances rather than guessed.

criteria.model: Every agent count in the published size guide cites a recorded run on a real GCP VM of that machine type in which that many agents ran the stated workload with zero out-of-memory kills.
criteria.bar: Every agent count in the published size guide cites a recorded run on a real GCP VM of that machine type in which that many agents ran the stated workload with zero out-of-memory kills.
criteria.method: For each size-guide row, open the cited run record from the benchmark results and check machine type, agent count, workload profile and the out-of-memory kill counter.
criteria.driftMarkers: A size-guide agent count has no recorded GCP run behind it, or its cited run shows an out-of-memory kill.

criteria.title: The cost model answers the 10x question

intent.request: Find a way to cut the cost of 50 agents by 10x, measured against the customer price.

criteria.model: The cost model states, for each tested lever combination, the measured Google cost per month for 50 agents and whether it is at or below the D-003 target of about $80/month.
criteria.bar: The cost model states, for each tested lever combination, the measured Google cost per month for 50 agents and whether it is at or below the D-003 target of about $80/month.
criteria.method: Read the P-012 cost model and trace each combination's figure to its capacity run and the GCP list price used.
criteria.driftMarkers: A tested lever combination has no monthly cost figure for 50 agents, or its figure is not derived from a measured capacity run.

criteria.title: The memory ideas are each measured

intent.request: Test whether swap, compressed memory or parking lets agents use less real RAM without raising cost, since agents are RAM-heavy and CPU-light.

criteria.model: Disk swap, zram and process-free parking each have a recorded run reporting agents per GB of RAM and the wake delay when agents resume.
criteria.bar: Disk swap, zram and process-free parking each have a recorded run reporting agents per GB of RAM and the wake delay when agents resume.
criteria.method: Check the P-014, P-015 and P-009 run records for both measurements.
criteria.driftMarkers: Any of disk swap, zram or process-free parking has no recorded run with both agents-per-GB and wake delay.

criteria.title: Light and heavy users get a sizing and billing answer

intent.request: Decide whether to scale the machine automatically with usage and how to bill a 1-agent user versus a 50-agent user.

criteria.model: The P-012 recommendation states whether machines resize automatically and gives the monthly price for a 1-agent user and for a 50-agent user, each backed by measured cost.
criteria.bar: The P-012 recommendation states whether machines resize automatically and gives the monthly price for a 1-agent user and for a 50-agent user, each backed by measured cost.
criteria.method: Read the P-012 recommendation for the resize decision and both prices with their source runs.
criteria.driftMarkers: The recommendation omits the resize decision or either user's monthly price.

criteria.title: Test spending stays under $200 and no machine is left running

intent.request: Keep total Google Cloud spend for the tests at or under $200.

criteria.model: Billed spend on the test project for this plan is at or below $200, and after the last run no VM labelled for this plan exists.
criteria.bar: Billed spend on the test project for this plan is at or below $200, and after the last run no VM labelled for this plan exists.
criteria.method: Read the project's billing report for the plan label and list compute instances with that label after the final run.
criteria.driftMarkers: Billed spend exceeds $200, or a VM labelled for this plan still exists after the final run.

criteria.title: Real-VM placement preserves exclusive tenant assignment

intent.request: Real-VM placement preserves exclusive tenant assignment

acceptance.condition: Each initial placement or returning-workspace wake atomically reserves one eligible, compatible, clean and exclusively tenant-owned ordinary GCP/AWS VM or returns an explicit queued/refused result.
acceptance.falsifier: A stale, draining, incompatible or foreign-owned VM is selected, or two active customer leases share a VM.

verification.method: Run the pool selector and isolated database reservation concurrency/RLS tests, including duplicate wakes and stale generation conflicts.

criteria.title: Reconnect uses the same durable customer data

intent.request: Reconnect uses the same durable customer data

acceptance.condition: A workspace is published ready after idle wake or same-zone replacement only after exclusive writer fencing and confirmation of stable workspace identity, the expected encrypted data volume, correct tenant marker, acknowledged data hashes and connector readiness.
acceptance.falsifier: A blank/wrong-tenant volume mounts, the old writer remains unfenced, or ready is reported before data validation.

verification.method: Run real provider stop/start and replacement drills with hashes written before shutdown and read after reconnect; inject detach/attach timeouts.

criteria.title: Tenant boundaries and clean host reuse hold

intent.request: Tenant boundaries and clean host reuse hold

acceptance.condition: A caller can operate on a workspace host and its storage only while holding the current exclusive tenant authority for a cleanly provisioned or provably reimaged host with prior credentials and connector authority revoked.
acceptance.falsifier: A cross-tenant operation succeeds or a previously assigned unclean VM is admitted to another customer.

verification.method: Run isolated-DB RLS, cross-tenant route, credential-revocation and clean-host eligibility tests plus an internal canary.

criteria.title: Trial and paid policy controls resources

intent.request: Trial and paid policy controls resources

acceptance.condition: Each hosted lifecycle action is admitted only when it satisfies canonical server-owned concurrency, storage, idle, paid-reservation and spend policy together with active-work, viewer and in-flight-operation safety holds.
acceptance.falsifier: Caller labels raise entitlements, active work is stopped, or pending reservations escape limits.

verification.method: Run policy, duplicate admission, budget, viewer, overload/fairness and upgrade/downgrade tests using existing lifecycle surfaces.

acceptance.condition: For each infrastructure billing period, tenant charges plus explicit shared overhead and unresolved-rate allocations reconcile exactly to the input total across compute, retained storage, provisioned performance, backup, network, control-plane and warm capacity using achieved agent capacity.
acceptance.falsifier: Allocated tenant cost plus explicit overhead differs from the input bill, a missing rate becomes zero, or nominal slots replace achieved capacity.

verification.method: Run cost-model tests for 1/50 agents, zero activity, warm overhead, mixed providers, credits, currency mismatch and unknown rates. Verify the report separately presents working base-plus-agent and busy-hours alternatives and identifies inference costs separately, without treating unknown rates as zero.

acceptance.condition: Each queued-demand reconciliation makes at most one budgeted, generation-fenced capacity change through the existing durable workflows after counting pending hosts and checking cooldown, fresh observations, safe drain and demonstrated reclaim recovery before spot use.
acceptance.falsifier: A second scheduler is introduced, duplicate provision occurs, an active host is retired or an unknown observation silently permits action.

verification.method: Run replay, reservation contention, cooldown, quota, failed-provision cleanup and lifecycle integration tests.

acceptance.condition: Internal canaries demonstrate database-consistent backup/restore, retained-data recovery and provider-confirmed cleanup under a bounded budget before external customer enrollment.
acceptance.falsifier: Backup is claimed from an unconfirmed snapshot, recovery loses acknowledged canary data or a billable canary resource remains unaccounted.

verification.method: Use existing snapshot/restore and resource-obligation ledgers; record backup recovery, before/after markers and final provider inventory.

criteria.title: Shipment is tied to the deployed artifact

intent.request: Shipment is tied to the deployed artifact

acceptance.condition: The real-VM hybrid-pool customer journey passes on the exact shipped green artifact with recorded runtime identity, wake/reconnect evidence, policy/isolation assertions and rollback path.
acceptance.falsifier: Only shaping, unit tests, staging source or a deployment request is cited as proof of shipment.

verification.method: Read pipeline/artifact identity and exercise the shipped customer journey; preserve the deployment, canary, cost and teardown receipts.

amendment.reason: Reconcile revision185 R1–R5 with owner-authorized hybrid plan216. Preserve original five BARs verbatim. New R6–R13 retain all authored guarantees and Design evidence planes; R6–R11 now express a single observable admit/ready/authority/conservation/reconciliation behavior with explicit preconditions, complying with the canonical atomicity guard. No acceptance or shipment claim; P544 D076 all-in usable under-$20 remains open.
